en: any (with a negative: no ... at all)

examples.en: I didn't go anywhere over the weekend.
I'm hungry. Anything is fine, please.

explain: ‘아무’ 뒤에는 보통 ‘도’나 ‘나’가 붙어요. 아무도 + 부정 = 한 명도 없다, 아무나 = 누구든지.

dict_examples.ko: 아무 의사라도 좋으니 빨리 좀 모셔 오세요.
dict_examples.en: Any doctor will do, so please fetch one quickly.

dict_examples.en: You must not meet just anybody.

dict_examples.ko: 밤이 되자 두 사람은 아무 데고 드러누웠다.
dict_examples.en: When night came, the two lay down anywhere.

explain_en: 아무 is usually followed by 도 or 나. 아무도 + a negative means “no one at all”, and 아무나 means “anyone”.

p.n: 하등 is formal and literary and only goes with a negative; 아무 is neutral and also works in 아무나, 아무도.

examples.en: The meeting time was announced in the team group chat.

examples.ko: 단체방에 사진을 올렸더니 다들 한마디씩 했어요.
examples.en: When I posted a photo in the group chat, everyone had something to say.

examples.ko: 개인적인 이야기는 단체방 말고 따로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please send personal matters separately, not in the group chat.

examples.ko: 부서 단체방에서는 중요한 공지를 놓치지 않도록 알림을 켜 둡니다.
examples.en: In the department group chat, I keep notifications on so I don't miss important notices.
As soon as I was invited to the group chat, I had to introduce myself.

explain: '단체방'은 세 명 이상이 함께 있는 대화방이에요. '단톡방'이라고도 많이 말해요. 회사에서는 부서나 팀마다 단체방을 따로 만드는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: 단체방 is a chat with three or more people. 단톡방 is also very common. Companies often make a separate one for each department or team.

en: to be fun; to be enjoyable

examples.en: If you know any fun books, please recommend one.
Studying Korean is getting more fun.
I signed up because it seemed more fun than I expected.

explain: '재미있다'의 준말로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 반대는 '재미없다'이고 '재밌없다'는 틀린 말이에요. '웃기다'는 웃음이 나오는 일에만 쓰지만, '재밌다'는 웃기지 않아도 흥미롭고 즐거울 때 써요.
explain_en: It is the contracted form of '재미있다' and is used more in speech. The opposite is '재미없다'; '재밌없다' is wrong. '웃기다' is only for things that make you laugh, but '재밌다' also covers things that are simply interesting and enjoyable.

p.n: Same meaning. 재미있다 is the full form and a bit more neutral in writing.
